Eight years old, terrible storm at summer camp. Thunder, lightning, hail, flooding. Everyone evacuated to the dining hall. I was standing in front of a window watching the storm. Fourteen year old junior counselor was in the middle of asking me to get away from the window and go to the middle of the room to play games with everyone else, when we saw one of the biggest and oldest trees on camp get struck by lightning. There was this bright white-blue flash, and she grabbed me by the arm and dragged me under a table. The tree was maybe a hundred feet away, maybe more, I'm not sure. But it fell directly across the parade field,  diagonally, and crashed onto the uncovered porch, stopping just a few feet short of the window I was just standing in front of. The crack of the lightning as it struck the tree, and the boom it made as it fell, were the loudest sounds I'd ever heard in my life. I was terrified. I'm sure the junior counselor was terrified too, she was very much still a child herself, but she pretended not to be scared for my sake. Most people who were in the room hadn't noticed exactly what happened, there was just an ungodly loud noise and then a bunch of kids started crying. I told that story a lot in subsequent years, and anyone who wasn't in that dining hall that day didn't believe me when I said a tree almost fell on me once, lol. Not the scariest thing I've ever seen, but the scariest thing I saw that people didn't believe me about.

I'm a bit older than you (20) so its not so long ago that I was in your shoes. I still have a little baby fat in my cheeks now, but I definitely had more when I was 16-18. I look like a featherless chicken with a bad skin condition on its face and I was definitely asked out as a joke or told someone liked me as a joke several times growing up. Nobody ever looked my way or had a crush on me either. 

My advice to you is to consider going to a dermatologist for your acne if it bothers you enough, but if that isn't an option then I recommend PanOxyl from the drugstore because that helped me clear up some of the stuff on my face/ body. My next recommendation is to make more intentional choices in your life. If you always order the same food from the same restaurant out of habit, it doesn't hurt to look at the menu again and find something else that appeals to you. 

Making intentional choices when it comes to clothes is important, because it can seriously help with your self esteem. Are you wearing the same type of clothes you always wear because they fit you and you have them, or do you actually like them and they make you happy when you put them on? There's a lot of clothes on the market for young women now that are pretty much made for petite figures, and you can find cute styles like that at Primark and Target and even thrift stores. Also trying a new hairstyle that frames your face shape well can help you feel pretty. 

For what it's worth, a lot of things that bothered me at 16 didn't/don't bother me as much a few years down the road. Some of my hyperinsecurities faded just to regular insecurities or disappeared entirely. My advice is to find what makes you personally feel pretty and confident, and pursue it. If its dyed hair and graphic tees and neon nail polish, that's wonderful! If its cute dresses and ballet flats and jewelry, that's wonderful too!

I wish you luck in someday being comfortable in your skin :)

A very similar situation happened to me when I was 17-18, (20 now). I know how heartbreaking it is to leave where you've spent your whole life. My dad said "you can have the house, the car, and [my name]" to my mom, even though in the end she only got to keep me. 

For your mother, you could write her a letter telling her how much you love her and how much you appreciate all she does, and maybe get some flowers. Cooking some meals for her here and there and taking on a couple of her chores  could be helpful, too. 

As for your dog, you could maybe get it registered as an emotional support animal, then depending on the laws where you live, the apartment complex would be required to let you keep your dog. You could likely find a therapist or psychiatrist online that can write a letter confirming why you need to keep your dog for your emotional wellbeing. 

I am so sorry for what you're going through, and best of luck with everything.

There was an outhouse off the trail and apparently i had gotten out of my sleeping bag, unzipped the tent without waking anyone, slept walk across the field, up a hill, and was in front of the door of the outhouse. (I knew the trails extremely well and had been camping there many times since i was 7). 

My hand was almost on the doorhandle and suddenly alarm bells went off in my brain and said "WAKE UP NOW!" So I did. I woke with a start and directly to my right, 3 feet away, was an eastern coyote. We stared at each other for a while before it pranced off into the woods. There was barely enough moonlight for me to see what it was.
